prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision: Build a fair, free, open society; put wellbeing, opportunity and environmental sustainability at the heart of government.

Stop Brexit: Revoke Article 50 if winning a majority; otherwise back a People’s Vote with the option to remain. Use a £50bn “Remain Bonus” to invest in public services and tackle inequality. Protect freedom of movement, EU citizens’ rights and Gibraltar’s status.

Economy and work:
- Invest £130bn in infrastructure (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing) and £5bn for a Green Investment Bank; nationwide fibre broadband.
- Rebalance regions via a £50bn programme and local banking; expand the British Business Bank.
- Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; strengthen innovation clusters and creative industries.
- Tech ethics: a Lovelace Code, stronger data oversight, consumer rights on data.
- Small business: start-up allowance; prompt payment enforcement; high street and town centre support.
- Fair taxes: restore corporation tax to 20%; replace business rates with a land value levy; clamp down on multinational tax avoidance and improve the Digital Services Tax.
- Future of work: day-one flexible working; new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; higher minimum wage for zero-hours at normal demand; right to fixed hours after 12 months; stronger enforcement; union access; plan for a genuine Living Wage.
- Lifelong learning: £10,000 Skills Wallet for every adult; reform apprenticeship levy; expand higher vocational routes.

Education and families:
- Free, high-quality childcare from 9 months for working parents (35 hours, 48 weeks); tripled Early Years Pupil Premium; £1bn for Children’s Centres.
- Reverse school cuts; 20,000 extra teachers; fix buildings; fund SEND; scrap SATs and league tables; replace Ofsted; introduce a broad “curriculum for life”; protect arts.
- FE/HE: +£1bn for colleges, maintenance grants restored, stronger mental health support, Young People’s Premium.

Climate, nature and transport:
- Net zero by 2045; 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking; £6bn/year ramp-up for home insulation; zero‑carbon new homes by 2021; circular economy law and plastics bans; plant 60m trees/year; protect peatlands, rivers and 50% of UK waters; £5bn for flood resilience.
- Transport: Clean Air Act; EV-only new cars by 2030; more chargers; shift freight to rail; restore bus routes (£4.5bn); major cycling/walking investment; rail electrification by 2035; freeze commuter fares; reform franchising; support HS2/NPR with tighter controls.

Health and social care:
- 1p on income tax raising £7bn/yr for NHS and social care; £10bn capital programme.
- Mental health: new waiting time standards; expand talking therapies; 24/7 crisis services and hospital liaison; perinatal support; implement Mental Health Act reforms; free prescriptions for chronic MH conditions.
- Workforce plan, GP access improvements, targeted bursaries; stronger support for carers; free end‑of‑life social care progression.
- Public health: obesity strategy, tobacco levy, air quality rights, PrEP access; drug reform including a regulated cannabis market; decriminalise abortion UK‑wide and create safe access zones.

Fair society, housing, justice:
- Welfare: cut UC wait to 5 days; scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; raise work allowances; fairer disability assessments; end sanctions regime; raise Local Housing Allowance.
- Housing: 300k homes/year incl. 100k social; zero‑carbon standards; Rent to Own; longer tenancies; tougher landlord licensing; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Policing and justice: £1bn for community policing; public health approach to violence; £500m for youth services; new Online Crime Agency; presumption against short prison sentences; rehabilitative prisons; Women’s Justice Board.

Rights, equality, immigration:
- Defend Human Rights Act/ECHR; restore Legal Aid; halt police facial recognition; modernise gender recognition (incl. non-binary/X); tackle hate crime; end period poverty; drive workplace diversity.
- Immigration: end hostile environment; 28‑day detention limit; move visa policy out of Home Office; merit‑based work visas; 2‑year post‑study work; scrap spouse income rule; cheaper child citizenship.
- Asylum: right to work after 3 months; resettle 10,000 refugees/year and 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years.

Political reform and devolution:
- Proportional representation (STV); votes at 16; automatic voter registration; reform Lords; citizens’ assemblies; stronger media standards and ad transparency.
- Federal UK with a written constitution; devolve powers and funding to nations/regions; protect and deepen devolution.

Global:
- Pro‑EU, pro‑multilateralism; 0.7% aid with more on climate; Magnitsky-style sanctions; stricter arms controls (suspend sales to Saudi); recognise Palestine; NATO 2% defence, cyber focus, minimum nuclear deterrent; support Hong Kong BNOs; lead global climate action.
